Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier today. To follow up, PayGrid would like to understand how open models compare to our in-house baseline (PayGrid-Base-v2) across our eval suite and what it would take to reach parity. A few specifics from our side: 

- Our acceptance threshold is roughly 0.95 on the weighted QA quality metric we discussed (precision-oriented but with recall floor of 0.85).
- We care about per-request latency (target < 350ms 95th) and inference cost (we typically budget ~$2k / month per high-traffic endpoint during pilot).
- I've attached the prompt set we used (paygrid_prompt_set_v3.jsonl) and a short README describing evaluation labels.

Can you share:
- Preliminary model recommendations (open models you think are promising) and any public/internal benchmark summaries you have.
- Expected gaps vs our baseline and levers to close them (prompting, instruction-tuning, lightweight finetune).
- A proposed next-step plan and rough timing for a side-by-side eval run.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with our engineering lead.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of ML Platform, PayGrid

Hi Alice / Tom —

Great talking earlier — thanks for sending the prompt set. Quick summary and proposed plan below. I’m copying our solutions lead Aditya to run the PayGrid prompts against our recent eval runs and Marcus for pricing/ops.

Top-line model recommendations (open-first approach):
- Llama-2-70B-chat (open): strongest out-of-the-box quality on QA/dialogue; on Redwood internal evals shows ~0.93 weighted QA vs PayGrid-Base-v2 at ~0.95.
- Redwood-curated-13B-quantized (open + optimizations): smaller but tuned quantized variant; ~0.94 on our weighted metric with much lower cost/latency.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (open): good cost/latency profile but lower quality (~0.88).

Caveats & levers to close the gap:
- Prompt engineering: we often see +0.5–1.5% in weighted quality with targeted prompt designs for domain-specific QA.
- Instruction-tuning / LoRA: lightweight tuning with ~5–10k examples typically yields +2–4% depending on task distribution.
- Canary & fallback routing: run primary on 13B-quantized with automatic fallback to 70B-chat for borderline queries to meet quality SLOs while controlling spend.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Redwood runs your prompt set on the three candidate models (Llama-2-70B-chat, Redwood-13B-quantized, Mistral-7B) and shares a comparative report (by EOD next business day). Attachment: preliminary benchmark summary (stub).
2) If results are close to parity, propose a 2-week canary with routing + monitoring; otherwise propose a short LoRA run (~1–2 weeks) and repeat.

Can you confirm the acceptance metric (0.95 weighted QA) and whether latency/cost hard floors are absolute or flexible for the pilot?

Attachments: paygrid-benchmark-report-20260328.pdf (summary stub), redwood-model-recs.xlsx

Best,

Marissa — quick notes from the runs I kicked off overnight and a few technical observations: 

Run details (prompt conditioning = paygrid_prompt_set_v3, sequence length ~512):
- Llama-2-70B-chat: weighted QA = 0.928; precision = 0.94; recall = 0.87; 95th latency = 410ms (on p4d equiv).
- Redwood-13B-quantized: weighted QA = 0.941; precision = 0.92; recall = 0.89; 95th latency = 220ms.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct: weighted QA = 0.881; precision = 0.89; recall = 0.80; 95th latency = 180ms.

Interpretation & levers: 
- The 13B-quantized is surprisingly close to parity and hits your latency target easily; cost is materially lower. The 70B still slightly trails on weighted QA but has higher precision on certain conversational edge-cases.
- Prompt tuning alone got us ~+0.6% vs off-the-shelf prompts across a small held-out dev set.
- Lightweight LoRA (5k examples) is projected to add +2–3% for 13B, +1–2% for 70B depending on label noise.

Operational tradeoffs:
- Canary suggestion: default to 13B-quantized with a confidence-based fallback to 70B-chat for queries with low model confidence or high-risk categories. That preserves latency/cost while keeping quality near parity.

I’ve uploaded the per-example output and scoring to the Drive folder and filled the attached sheet with the numbers. Will stand by to run a LoRA trial if you want to propose that.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
